name: frontend
description: Family Greenhouse web app — React + TypeScript + Vite PWA for collaborative household plant care.

scripts.build: tsc -b && vite build && vite build --ssr src/entry-server.tsx --outDir dist-ssr && node scripts/prerender.mjs

_size-limit-note: Budgets are REGRESSION GATES set ~8% above the current measured size (brotli), not aspirational targets — the old values (40/60/230/10) were below what the app has ever shipped, so the check was permanently red and gated nothing. Trimming the bundle further (the index chunk and Tailwind CSS are the candidates) is tracked as future work for when real-device Lighthouse data shows it matters. Keep these tight: lower them whenever a real reduction lands. Measured with @size-limit/file (brotli) only — the preset-app 'time' plugin ran headless Chrome to estimate JS execution time, gated nothing (no time budgets), and broke CI+local runs with puppeteer navigation timeouts. Vendor budget raised 51 → 64 kB for the React 18 → 19 upgrade: react-dom 19 is ~12 kB (brotli) larger than 18, putting the React runtime chunk at ~59.5 kB measured — a sanctioned, unavoidable dependency increase, not regression drift; 64 kB keeps the usual ~8% headroom. All-JS-combined budget raised 312 → 320 kB when the care-guide content surface grew (six new species pages + two blog posts): the prose lands in the lazy careGuides/BlogPost chunks, so the Initial JS and Vendor budgets are untouched — only the combined aggregate moved, to ~312.4 kB measured. This is sanctioned content growth, not regression drift; 320 kB keeps a tight ~2.5% cushion. All-JS-combined budget raised 320 → 330 kB for the v0.8.0 feature backlog (annual + lifetime billing UI, the no-care-data notice, server-confirmed analytics): the additions land in the lazy billing/settings and feature chunks, so the Initial JS (~60.4 kB) and Vendor budgets keep healthy headroom and only the aggregate moved, to ~320.1 kB measured — sanctioned growth, not regression drift; 330 kB restores a tight ~3% cushion. The v0.15.0 name nursery plus the already-merged React Router 7 runtime moved the measured aggregate to 331 kB while keeping initial JS at 47.3 kB; 340 kB restores a tight 2.7% regression cushion. All-JS-combined raised 340 → 348 kB for the Capacitor mobile shells: the @capacitor/core + push-notifications runtime lands in a lazy chunk that is dynamically imported ONLY inside the iOS/Android apps (web platform detection reads the injected window.Capacitor global precisely so web visitors never fetch it — see src/lib/platform.ts), moving the aggregate to ~337.7 kB measured while Initial JS (48.7 kB) and Vendor budgets are untouched; 348 kB keeps a tight ~3% cushion.
_size-limit-note-0-17: All-JS-combined raised 348 → 360 kB for the location-aware plant move workflow: the 349.39 kB measured aggregate includes the new 2.71 kB-gzip MovePlantsDialog lazy chunk, while Initial JS (11.88 kB), Vendor (61.32 kB), and CSS (14.59 kB) remain within their existing budgets. _size-limit-note-blog-expansion: All-JS-combined raised 386 -> 402 kB for the blog content expansion (eight new posts: shared-household care, travel/plant-sitter handover, and the overwatering / yellow-leaves / room-light diagnostics). Every word lands in the lazy `posts` chunk that only /blog/:slug pulls, so no critical-path budget moved: Initial JS 14.6 kB (limit 62), Vendor 59.85 kB (limit 64), CSS 12.5 kB (limit 15) are all unchanged. _size-limit-note-help-content: All-JS-combined raised 402 -> 435 kB, sized once for the two content surfaces landing together: the nine public /help/:topicId pages (this branch, #389) and the 14 species care guides (#384). Measured on a post-#391 build, which is the only build that counts here - prerendering changed the emitted output and moved the main baseline 389.69 -> 394.57 kB, so every earlier reading is stale. Against that baseline: help alone 405.22 kB (+10.65), care guides alone 411.6 kB (+17.03), both together 422.25 kB (+27.68) measured. 435 kB is 3.0% over the combined figure, the usual cushion, and both branches carry the same value so it is merge-order independent. This supersedes an earlier note on this branch claiming a 386 -> 397 kB raise: main never sat at 397, the branch inherited 402 from #383, and 397 would not have held the measured size in any case. The growth is the help answers themselves - helpContent is a 61.95 kB raw chunk that only /help and /help/:topicId pull, and App.tsx already lazy-loads both routes. Lazy-loading bounds what a visitor downloads, not this budget: `dist/assets/*.js` globs all 97 emitted chunks, so splitting cannot move this number, which is why #383 raised the limit for the blog posts while correctly calling them lazy. Nine public help pages earn it: they are the pages that answer 'how do I cancel' and 'I cannot log in' for signed-out users, they are prerendered to real HTML for search, and each answer carries a plain-text twin that feeds the FAQPage JSON-LD. No critical-path budget moved: Initial JS 15.63 kB (limit 62), Vendor 59.93 kB (limit 64), CSS 12.6 kB (limit 15), against 15.6 / 59.98 / 12.52 on main - flat to within 80 B, and not one of those three limits is relaxed. Sanctioned content growth, not regression drift.
_size-limit-note-0-23-legal-i18n: Legal-page i18n move: no budget change, but the cushion is now thin. The privacy, terms, support and account-deletion prose moved into the i18n catalogs (101 keys x 2 locales), growing the startup i18n chunk 122.07 -> 158.91 kB raw (33.80 -> 43.97 kB brotli) and the measured All-JS-combined aggregate 423.05 -> 433.15 kB brotli (+10.10). Re-measured against main after #389 (public help pages), #390 (payments-live legal corrections) and #384 (14 care guides) had all landed; the earlier reading on this branch (375.91 -> 386.26 kB, proposing a 386 -> 398 kB raise) predates all three and is stale, and the 402 -> 435 hunk it carried is now a no-op because main already sits at 435. This branch therefore raises nothing and relaxes nothing: 435 kB, set by #389 and #384 for the help and care-guide content surfaces, still holds. It holds by 1.85 kB - a 0.43% cushion, not the ~3% this file usually keeps - because 435 was sized for those two content surfaces and did not budget for this catalog growth on top. Read that as a real signal, not a rounding error: the next content or catalog addition will breach it, and the fix is the deferred work below rather than another raise. No critical-path budget moved: Initial JS 15.63 kB (limit 62, against 15.66 on main), Vendor 59.93 kB (limit 64, unchanged), CSS 12.6 kB (limit 15, unchanged). Unlike the lazy pricing/help/care chunks, both catalogs load at startup by design, so this 10 kB lands on every visit even though Spanish is still gated off; the follow-up is a lazily-added `legal` namespace (i18n.addResourceBundle from the legal routes) that would return it to the startup path and restore the cushion without touching the limit.
_size-limit-note-0-23-calendar-feed: All-JS-combined raised 435 -> 450 kB for the revocable calendar-feed link, and to clear an overage main was already carrying. Both readings were taken in one worktree with one npm ci, same tree and same node_modules, on this branch rebased onto main at 5d3c5be. Main alone measures 435.89 kB and is ALREADY 893 B over the 435 kB limit: the gate went red on main itself when #394 (onboarding activation) landed, and CI's own Bundle size run on adf2e53 reports that identical 435.89 kB / 893 B pair, so this is main's drift reproduced, not a local artifact. This branch measures 437.53 kB, so its own contribution is 1.64 kB and it is exactly where this feature should land: +944 B in the startup i18n chunk (27 new keys x en + es) and +667 B in the lazy AccountSettings chunk (the mint / reveal-once / revoke / regenerate UI plus calendarFeedService). Every other chunk moves by tens of bytes of hashing noise and no new chunk is emitted. No critical-path budget moved - Initial JS 15.66 kB (limit 62), Vendor 59.94 kB (limit 64) and CSS 12.6 kB (limit 15) are byte-identical on main and on this branch. 450 kB is 2.9% over the measured 437.53 kB, restoring the ~3% cushion that the note above recorded falling to 0.43%. Most of what this raise buys back is main's, not this branch's: the deferred lazy `legal` namespace described in that note is still the real fix for the startup i18n chunk, and it is now overdue - the next content or catalog addition should land it rather than take another raise.
_size-limit-note-0-23-deferred-legal-cat: Deferred legal catalog: NO budget change, and a measurement that closes out the follow-up the two notes above kept deferring. `_size-limit-note-0-23-legal-i18n` named the fix (a lazily-added `legal` namespace via i18n.addResourceBundle from the legal routes) and `_size-limit-note-0-23-calendar-feed` called it overdue. This is that fix. THE MOVE: the 101 privacy/terms/support/account-deletion keys per locale left `locales/<lng>/translation.json` for `locales/<lng>/legal.json`, which src/i18n/legalCatalog.ts merges into the `translation` namespace with addResourceBundle, on demand, from the four legal routes only. App.tsx awaits that load inside each route's React.lazy() factory, in parallel with the page chunk, so the copy is registered before the component mounts - on navigation, on hydration of a prerendered page, and in the build-time prerender, whose react-dom/static prerender() waits on the same promise. /legal/privacy and /legal/terms come out of the prerender byte-identical to main, asset hashes aside (8,513 and 4,301 characters of prose, zero raw keys). Keys are unchanged and still `legal.*`-rooted, so no call site moved, and check-i18n-catalogs.mjs gates both files (NAMESPACES is now ['translation','legal']): 875 en / 894 es keys before and after, none dropped. WHAT IT BOUGHT, AND WHERE: the startup i18n chunk fell 175.93 -> 139.10 kB raw and 48.30 -> 38.20 kB brotli. Every visit now ships 36.83 kB raw / 10.11 kB brotli less, in both locales, including a build where Spanish is still gated off; net of the loader and lazy wrapper (+138 B on Initial JS) that is 9.97 kB brotli off the startup path for every visitor. WHAT IT DID NOT BUY, MEASURED: the All-JS-combined aggregate did not fall. It rose, 444.06 -> 444.88 kB (+827 B). `All-JS-combined` globs dist/assets/*.js - all 99 emitted chunks - and @size-limit/file brotli-compresses each file separately and sums them, so the same prose costs MORE once it has its own chunk (10.83 kB standalone) than it did interleaved in a large shared one (10.11 kB in-context). `_size-limit-note-help-content` already said splitting cannot lower this number; this is the measurement showing it raises it slightly, and it corrects the expectation in the two notes above that a deferred namespace would restore this budget's cushion. It cannot, and no further split of this catalog will: this budget counts bytes emitted, not bytes downloaded, so the win is real but lands somewhere this gate does not look. Read that as a property of the gate, not a reason to skip the fix - and as a limit on what this budget is for. It is a good regression gate on total emitted JS and a blind one on delivery: any work that moves bytes off the startup path without deleting them (deferred namespaces, route-scoped catalogs, on-demand chunks) will look flat or slightly negative here while being a real win for users. Judge that class of change on the startup-chunk figures recorded above, not on this number, and do not let a flat aggregate argue against doing it. NO LIMIT MOVES: 450 kB, set by #399, still holds - 444.88 kB measured leaves a 1.14% cushion where main already sat at 1.34%, so this branch spends 827 B of an existing cushion and neither raises nor lowers anything. Lowering the limit was considered and is not supported by the measurement. No critical-path budget moves either - Initial JS 15.83 kB (limit 62, against 15.69 on main), Vendor 60.01 kB (limit 64, unchanged), CSS 12.66 kB (limit 15, unchanged). Measured with `npm ci && cd frontend && npm run build && npm run size`, main and branch back to back in one worktree on one node_modules, Node 26.8.1 / npm 11.19.0; main reads 444.06 kB here, the same figure #420 reported, so this pair is reproducible across environments rather than a local artifact. ONE INTERACTION TO WATCH: PR #419 (not on main as of 55832fa) pins `src/i18n/locales/` to a named `i18n` chunk in vite.config.ts. As written that rule also captures locales/<lng>/legal.json and folds the prose back into a modulepreloaded chunk - measured, the deferred chunk collapses to 154 B - silently undoing this split while every test stays green. tests/unit/i18n/legalCatalog.test.ts fails loudly if that rule lands without excluding the legal fragments.
_size-limit-note-double-care: All-JS-combined raised 450 -> 470 kB for double-care detection and schedule drift (#423). Measured 2026-09-04 with this branch rebased onto main at f484634 (#428, the deferred legal catalog, on top of #420 Away Kit and #421 kiosk): main alone builds to 449.8 kB brotlied and this branch to 451.43 kB, so the feature costs +1.63 kB. Both readings were taken in one worktree from one npm ci, same node_modules, `npm run build && npm run size` on each side. THE RAISE IS NOT ALL THIS BRANCH: main now measures 449.8 kB against its own 450 kB limit - 200 B of headroom - so 450 no longer holds main plus any feature at all, and #428 (which freed ~10 kB by lazy-loading the legal catalog) has already been spent. Earlier notes on this branch proposing a raise off a 435/437 kB baseline predate #399, #412, #420, #421 and #428 and are stale in every number. No critical-path budget moved: Initial JS 17.15 kB (limit 62), Vendor 59.91 kB (limit 64), CSS 12.79 kB (limit 15), against 15.88 / 59.91 / 12.79 on main, and not one of those three limits is relaxed. The growth is the feature itself: the DoubleCarePrompt, DoubleCareCard and ScheduleDriftHint surfaces plus ~40 new i18n keys across en + es. Lazy-loading cannot move this number (`dist/assets/*.js` globs every emitted chunk), which is why the aggregate moves and the critical-path budgets do not. 470 kB is the smallest round step that holds this measurement with a real cushion (4.11%). MERGE ORDER: #419, #423, #424 and #425 each measure over 450 on this same main and each carry this same 470 kB, so no one of them depends on landing first - but their deltas are additive (+3.39, +1.63, +10.73, +5.49) and the all-four aggregate projects to ~471 kB, which 470 will NOT hold. Every one of them after the first must re-measure on the new main rather than assume 470 still stands.
_size-limit-note-0-23-feature-wave: All-JS-combined raised 470 -> 515 kB, sized ONCE for the whole in-flight feature wave so that no individual PR in it has to raise it — the same thing `_size-limit-note-help-content` did when it sized a single raise for the two content surfaces landing together. Sixteen PRs in this wave each add 0-11 kB of frontend weight (#413 #414 #415 #416 #417 #418 #419 #422 #423 #424 #425 #427 #429 #431 #432 #433). They cannot all fit under one branch-sized ceiling, they have been failing `Bundle size` one after another (#431 by 1.06 kB and #422 by 1.28 kB in CI, both against 450), and each one raising the limit on its own rewrites this same JSON line and re-conflicts the whole queue. The note directly above is the proof: #423 merged mid-way through writing this one, carrying 450 -> 470 with it, so main moved 98b4439 -> 9e84de5 and every other branch's size hunk went stale again. Five of the remaining PRs still carry their own raise, between them proposing four different ceilings (#425 460, #432 465, #413 468, #419/#424 470 kB), and the bodies still argue for 439, 450, 452 and 454 on top of that. This PR is the one raise. Every other PR in the wave should drop its size hunk entirely and rebase onto this. MEASURED MAIN: `origin/main` at 9e84de5 measures 452.15 kB (452,151 B brotli, 101 emitted chunks) via `npm ci && cd frontend && npm run build && npm run size` on Node 26.8.1 / npm 11.19.0, darwin arm64. The same command on its parent 98b4439 read 449.80 kB, and CI — Node 22 on ubuntu — reported the identical 449.8 kB for that commit (run 33834448500). Worth naming the environment, because readings in this repo have moved ~1.4 kB between environments before and this pair does not. Critical path on 9e84de5: Initial JS 17.18 kB (limit 62), Vendor 59.91 kB (limit 64), CSS 12.79 kB (limit 15). HOW THE CUSHION KEEPS VANISHING, WHICH IS THE ARGUMENT FOR SIZING THIS ONCE: main measured 444.06 kB at 55832fa, 449.80 kB at 98b4439 and 452.15 kB at 9e84de5 — 8.1 kB of growth through merges alone (#421 kiosk, #428 deferred legal catalog, #430 billing emails, #423 double-care), while the limit sat at 450 through the first three of those. At 98b4439 the gate was green by 203 B, a 0.045% cushion, and #423 then had to raise it to merge at all. #403 recorded the same pattern at 435 and predicted it. A limit sized to fit one branch re-reds within a single merge cycle; that is the failure this raise exists to stop repeating. REMAINING PER-PR DELTAS: every row below was built in this one worktree on one `npm ci`, each branch tip measured against ITS OWN merge-base with main rather than against whatever main looked like when its PR body was written. Three bases cover the wave: 55832fa = 444.055 kB, f484634 = 98b4439 = 449.797 kB (#430 touched no frontend file, so main HEAD and its parent measured byte-identically), and 9e84de5 = 452.151 kB. #413 cross-home today +4.25 kB | #414 seasonal move day +1.31 | #415 identification top-up packs +2.33 | #416 member upgrade request + split the bill +4.03 | #417 coverage view +3.41 | #418 auto-handoff + rotation +2.35 | #419 away-kit recap + sitter photos +3.40 | #422 plan re-cut +1.49 | #424 qr plant tags +10.74 | #425 caretaker seats +8.07 | #427 reminder email 0.00 (no frontend file changed) | #429 terms refund/renewal language +2.53 | #431 household emails +1.27 | #432 html + text emails +0.41 | #433 email deliverability +0.68. #423 double-care measured +2.35 and has now merged, so its bytes are in the 452.15 kB baseline above rather than in this list. PROVENANCE, ROW BY ROW, because these numbers came from three places and two of them disagree. (a) All sixteen were measured here, at the head each PR carried when this note was written; #423, #424, #425 and #432 were re-measured after their heads were force-pushed mid-run, and the later reading is the one summed. (b) A second agent measured four of them back-to-back on the same 449.80 kB base. It agrees to the byte on #419 (453.19 kB) and on #424 (460.53 kB) — the strongest evidence here that these deltas are real and reproducible across runs. It read #423 at 451.43 (+1.63) and #425 at 455.29 (+5.49); both of those heads were force-pushed afterwards, and the current heads measure 452.15 (+2.35, since confirmed exactly by #423 landing on main) and 457.87 (+8.07). The larger, current figures are the ones summed — a budget should be sized off the branch that will actually merge. (c) CI corroborates independently on Node 22: #414 445.37, #417 447.46, #418 446.40, #429 446.59 and #427 448.92 kB, each exactly base-plus-delta, and the two red jobs (#431 over by 1.06 kB, #422 over by 1.28 kB) land on 451.06 and 451.28 kB, which is 449,797 B plus 1,266 B and plus 1,486 B — byte-exact. (d) Four PR bodies (#415, #416, #418, #429) stated no delta at all; the rest stated one, mostly against a main from before #421 and #428 landed. Not one was taken on trust, and where a body conflicts with a measurement, the measurement is what is summed. THE ARITHMETIC: 46,245 B (46.25 kB) of summed deltas for the fifteen PRs still to land, on top of 452,151 B measured, = 498,396 B, 498.40 kB projected once the whole wave is in. 515 kB is 3.33% over that — the cushion this file has kept since the 0.17 raise — and it is a round number in the series this file already uses (348 / 360 / 374 / 386 / 402 / 435 / 450 / 470). Note the projection does not move as the wave lands: when #423 merged, 2,354 B left the delta column and entered the baseline, and 498,396 B was the total before and after. That invariance is deliberate. This ceiling stays correct however many more of these merge while it is in review, and no rebase should recompute it. THESE DELTAS ADD UP, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE POINT: a limit chosen to fit one branch is wrong by construction, because the next branch lands on top of it. #419, #424 and #425 alone are +22.2 kB over today's main, so the four ceilings still being proposed (460 through 470) each hold for about one more merge. 46.25 kB on top of what has already landed is a large raise and it is stated plainly rather than trimmed to look modest: it is the honest cost of sixteen features, two fifths of it in just two of them (#424 print sheet and in-house QR encoder +10.74, #425 caretaker surfaces +8.07), and most of the remainder in new i18n keys across en + es. WHAT THIS TOTAL IS, AND IS NOT: it is a sum of deltas each measured in isolation, not a measurement of the merged tree, and it will not be exactly right in either direction. Brotli on a shared chunk is sub-additive — most of these PRs add keys to the same startup i18n chunk, so landing together should cost somewhat LESS than the sum — while rebases that shift chunk boundaries cost a little more, and #419 pins `src/i18n/locales/` to a named chunk, which re-chunks the catalogs for everyone. That spread is exactly what the 3% cushion is for. This is a budget, not a prediction. RE-TIGHTEN THIS ONCE THE WAVE HAS LANDED. 515 kB is a ceiling derived from arithmetic over sixteen branches, not a measurement of anything that exists yet. When the wave is in, measure main again and lower this number to the real post-wave figure plus the usual ~3%. Do not leave 515 standing as the permanent budget, and do not let the headroom it creates quietly absorb work that was never counted here. WHAT THIS GATE CANNOT SEE: #428 moved the 101 legal keys per locale to a deferred namespace and took 36.83 kB raw / 10.11 kB brotli off the startup chunk on EVERY visit — and All-JS-combined went UP 827 B, because it globs `dist/assets/*.js` and brotlis each emitted chunk separately, so the same prose costs more standing alone (10.83 kB) than interleaved in a large shared chunk (10.11 kB). This gate counts bytes EMITTED, not bytes DOWNLOADED. A number rising here therefore does not by itself mean the app got slower, and a flat number here does not mean a real delivery win did not happen. The critical-path signal is the Initial JS budget, and it is worth reading against this wave: every branch above sits comfortably inside its 62 kB limit except #419, which pins the i18n catalogs to their own chunk and moves Initial JS 15.88 -> 30.25 kB against its own merge-base — a +14.4 kB critical-path change carried by a PR whose aggregate delta here is only +3.40 kB. That is the same blindness running the other way. Judge that class of change on Initial JS, not on this budget. NO CRITICAL-PATH BUDGET MOVES HERE: Initial JS, Vendor and CSS keep their 62 / 64 / 15 kB limits untouched. This PR changes one limit and adds this note. There is no feature code in it.
_size-limit-note-away-kit-initial-js: Away Kit recap + sitter photo-back (#419): NO limit moves, and a measurement that retires the `i18n` chunk pin this branch was carrying. THE CLAIM UNDER TEST: an independent reading of this branch put `Initial JS` at 30.25 kB against 15.88 kB on main and read that as the branch nearly doubling the critical path. Reproduced exactly - 30,250 B - and then explained. TWO THINGS WERE TRUE AT ONCE. First, the pin was not the cost, it was the fix: at this branch's old base (98b44398) removing the pin entirely measures `Initial JS` 57.16 kB, because rollup folds both startup catalogs into the entry chunk. 30.25 was the pinned reading and 57.16 the unpinned one, so the correct counterfactual for the pin is -26.9 kB, not +14.4. Second, that whole swing is chunk boundaries moving, not bytes arriving: `Initial JS` globs dist/assets/index-*.js alone, while dist/index.html modulepreloads six more chunks (vendor, ui, query, api, authStore, i18n). Summing the entry script and every modulepreloaded sibling, brotlied the same way size-limit does it, the flip is 191.79 -> 191.94 kB. 148 bytes. The catalogs were downloaded before first paint either way; only the file they arrived in changed. `Initial JS` is a good gate on the entry chunk and a blind one on delivery, the same way `All-JS-combined` is a good gate on emitted bytes and a blind one on what is downloaded (see the deferred-legal-catalog note above). MEASURED ON CURRENT MAIN (9e84de5), one worktree, one npm ci, `npm run build && npm run size` back to back, Initial / All-JS / critical path in kB brotli: main alone 17.18 / 452.15 / 197.15; this branch with the old path-wide pin 17.92 / 455.43 / 197.77; with the pin removed entirely 17.91 / 455.70 / 198.04; with the pin narrowed to `locales/<lng>/translation.json` 17.92 / 455.43 / 197.77. The 14 kB is gone: it was never this branch's, it was the old base's chunk graph, and #423 landing dissolved it. What is left of the pin is 6 B more on `Initial JS` and 272 B LESS on the critical path than dropping it, so the pin is kept - narrowed. IS THE FLIP GONE OR QUIET? Quiet. Removing the pin and adding one more lazy route measures 17.93 kB, no flip, so nothing about today's graph is fragile - but the identical source flipped one merge ago and nothing in the build states the invariant, so the next merge can flip it back. The pin costs nothing and says it out loud, which is what the vendor/query/ui rules above already do for the same reason. NARROWED, NOT REMOVED: the rule now matches `locales/<lng>/translation.json` by name instead of matching the locales directory and excluding legal.json. Same bytes out (byte-identical build), but an allowlist cannot swallow the next deferred namespace the way the denylist swallowed #428's legal fragments, which needed an exclusion to be added after the fact. tests/unit/i18n/legalCatalog.test.ts now runs the config's own `/.../.test(id)` predicates against both filenames instead of grepping the file for the word `legal`, which a comment satisfied; it fails on a path-wide rule and passes on either correct shape. (It reads the config text rather than importing it: measured, a dynamic import of vite.config.ts inside vitest returns a stale copy that ignores edits, so an import-based version of that gate passes on a config it never read.) NO BUDGET MOVES: 62 / 64 / 515 / 15 kB are main's own values and all four pass - All-JS-combined measures 455.43 kB against the 515 kB #434 set for the whole wave. This branch deliberately carries NO size hunk of its own; the 450 -> 470 raise it used to carry was dropped rather than rebased, because a per-PR raise stacked on the wave-wide one is how 450 came to be spent four times over.
_size-limit-note-commercial-terms: All-JS-combined raised 515 -> 532 kB for the commercial terms the paid plans never had (#429): auto-renewal, cancellation, free trials, price changes and one-time purchases, in BOTH locales.
